patent.heading: Patent
patent.title: AI-Powered Personalized Multimedia Content Generation and Distribution System for Multi-Device Ecosystem
body: A system that generates multimedia tailored to an individual — text, images, audio and video assembled per person rather than produced once for everyone — and distributes it across the devices that person already uses.

The same underlying pattern, per-person generative media delivered across a multi-device ecosystem, is now appearing in products across several industries worldwide. The application was filed before that convergence was widely visible.

about.heading: About me
body: I'm a seasoned full-stack developer with over a decade of experience building web and mobile applications. Currently working at Amazon in Cupertino, California, I specialize in creating innovative AI-powered solutions, educational platforms, and business tools.

My passion lies in leveraging cutting-edge technologies to solve real-world problems, with a particular focus on AI/ML integration, children's education, and e-commerce solutions. I've successfully deployed 15+ production applications and built a portfolio of 29+ projects spanning multiple domains.

updates.heading: Latest updates
updates.intro: Signal pulled from LinkedIn — full text lives on the original post.

items.text: Running 10+ AI agents across 3 machines with zero unified visibility led me to build Orbit — one browser tab showing every live agent session, RAM usage, and a one-click kill switch across machines, persisted via tmux.

Built Paperclip Studio — a read-only 3D dashboard that turns a company of AI agents into a calm, glanceable scene: one character per agent, plain-English status, live activity feed. Zero dependencies, works on a phone. MIT-licensed, shipping hourly.
Reshared a look at real-world vertical integration — AI powering daily physical products while pushing sustainability goals forward.

A fun side experiment with Nano Banana AI: tried generating a consistent-character image sequence, and bananas crashed the party in 30–40% of the frames — including one car that ended up looking suspiciously like a banana.

writing.heading: Writing
writing.intro: Two posts on giving an AI assistant real control of a real app, both built on Raga Radio — my mood-filtered Indian classical station.

posts.coverAlt: A chat bubble containing an embedded audio player
posts.title: Putting a radio inside a chat
posts.note: An assistant can tell you Raga Multani suits the late afternoon. It cannot give you a seek bar. Shipping real UI from an MCP server with ui:// resources — and the CSP default that silently kills audio.

posts.coverAlt: A browser tab exposing two named tools to an agent
posts.title: Driving a tab you already have open
posts.note: The radio is already playing and you are already signed in. Letting the page publish its own tools on document.modelContext so any agent in the browser can drive it.
